semanticText:
# Bank Transfer Instruction

Represents one payer-requested bank transfer with separate guarantor acceptance and bank-outcome reporting. Its bank-transfer state can be installed before Activation is ready. A transfer request does not confirm money movement; completion records the guarantor’s bank confirmation. A refund is a separate transfer instruction.

## Terms and initialization

The type declares `paymentTerms.method: bank-transfer` and `paymentTerms.evidence: bankConfirmation`. `paymentTerms.amountMinor` is the full transfer amount in integer minor units of `paymentTerms.currency`. Payment initialization requires a positive amount, a nonempty currency, and an integer `paymentTerms.limitMinor` at least as large as the amount and no greater than 1,000,000,000,000.

Initialization also requires `paymentTerms.recipientApprovalRequired` to be Boolean. `paymentTerms.payerChannel` and `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel`, plus every entry in `paymentTerms.allowedPayees`, must name existing participant contracts using nonempty identifiers without `/` or `~`. An optional `paymentTerms.payeeChannel` defaults to an empty selection; a nonempty selection must belong to `allowedPayees`. These shared-ledger settings do not add a recipient-approval check to the bank-specific transfer operation.

The built-in `clauses.bankTransferState` uses the `state` pointer binding, defaulting to `/bankTransfer`. When clause installation creates that state, it supplies `status: idle`, `requestId: ""`, and `reference: ""`; an existing object is preserved. Bank operations themselves read `/bankTransfer` directly.

Payment initialization is separate. After `Clauses Initialized`, or on `Document Activated`, it runs only if `/payment/accepted` is absent and either there is no `clauses.activation` or `/activation/active` is true. It initializes acceptance and rejection flags to false, confirmed amounts to zero, and `transactionId` to an empty string, then emits `Payment Initialized` and `Payment Instruction Acceptance Requested` with `requestId: acceptance`. Missing fields are unknown, not implicit initialization defaults. All paths are local to this instruction’s document, including when it is nested.

## Operations and outcomes

The four bank workflows apply `Require Active Parties`. If `/activation` exists, they require active state, valid participant access, and a currently authorized calling channel. `requestTransfer` is bound to `payer` and checks the caller against `paymentTerms.payerChannel`; the three outcome operations are bound to `guarantor` and check `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel`.

The inherited `acceptPaymentInstruction` records guarantor acceptance and applies the active-party check. Its input may be empty or contain an optional text `reason`. `rejectPaymentInstruction` requires guarantor authority and a nonempty text `reason`; its workflow does not include that active-party step. Acceptance and rejection cannot replace one another. Repeating a decision requires the same recorded decision and reason. Instruction rejection is distinct from a later bank-transfer decline.

- `requestTransfer` accepts only `requestId`, a nonempty string of at most 128 characters. It requires `/payment/accepted` to be true. If `clauses.documentSources` exists, `/sourceLinks/ready` must be true. A new request also requires `/payment/closed` not to be true and, when `paymentTerms.transferGate` is present, the document value at that configured path to equal true. It records the identifier, sets `bankTransfer.status` to `requested`, and emits `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Requested`, using the amount and currency from `paymentTerms`.
- `confirmTransfer` requires the recorded `requestId`, a nonempty `reference` of at most 256 characters, and `amountMinor` and `currency` exactly matching `paymentTerms`. It sets status to `completed`, records the reference, sets `/payment/completed` to the full terms amount, and copies the reference to `/payment/transactionId`. It emits `Payment Completed` with `evidence: bankConfirmation`, followed by a `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Outcome`.
- `declineTransfer` and `reportTransferUnknown` require the same request correlation and reference constraints. They record `declined` or `unknown` and emit `Transfer Outcome` without increasing completed money. Their optional `amountMinor` and `currency` are not checked against the terms or stored by these operations. Outcome inputs allow only `requestId`, `reference`, `amountMinor`, and `currency`.

## Reconciliation and accounting

`idle` means no transfer request has been recorded after structural initialization. `requested` awaits the guarantor’s bank outcome; `unknown` awaits reconciliation against that same request. Either unresolved status can become `completed` or `declined`. Those two outcomes are final.

Once a request identifier is recorded, another identifier is rejected. Repeating the same identifier returns a duplicate without emitting another transfer request, after the source-readiness, caller and acceptance checks. Repeating an outcome requires the same status and reference; completion retries must still match the terms amount and currency. A different reference for the same status conflicts. Reconciliation from `unknown` to a final outcome may supply a new reference.

With the declared `bank-transfer` method, the inherited reservation-method guard rejects generic transaction initiation and financial or control request creation. This bank flow creates no synthetic authorization or capture. It uses `paymentTerms.amountMinor`, not the shared ledger’s `targetMinor`. `/payment/completed` records the confirmed transfer amount without subtracting refunds performed through separate instructions. Bank completion does not set `/payment/closed`, and a reference attached to an `unknown` or `declined` outcome is not confirmation of transferred money.
